The repository shell failed before any local read/write could occur (`bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`). I therefore could not update `research-ledger-manifest.json`; the additions below are the persistence handoff.

## 1B — Nuclear / catastrophic risk

- `BGD23-053`: Bangladesh’s official nuclear-safety report states that BAERA regulates Rooppur under the BAER Act, IAEA standards, licensing, inspection, enforcement, radiation protection, and emergency measures (2022 report, pp. 32–35). This establishes institutional safety posture, not personal Hasina conduct. [IAEA national report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/24/02/cns_bangladesh_national_report_2022.pdf)
- `BGD23-054`: The same report records the 2011 Bangladesh–Russia agreement for Russian fuel supply and spent-fuel return, government ownership, state-credit financing, and BAEC ownership. These are inherited policy arrangements still operative in 2023, not newly made 2023 decisions. [IAEA national report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/24/02/cns_bangladesh_national_report_2022.pdf)
- `BGD23-055`: Bangladesh received its first Russian uranium shipment in October 2023 for the under-construction Rooppur plant. [AP report](https://apnews.com/article/b38f3dcdce3404c3da0be1d68e7ba469)

Contrary/limitation: the IAEA review material also records a gap concerning Bangladesh’s political commitment to guidance on radioactive-source imports and disused-source management. [IAEA IRRS report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/documents/review-missions/final_irrs_report_bangladesh.pdf) No 2023 ruler-specific CBRN, biological, cyber, AI, or catastrophic-risk decision was recovered.

## 2B — International peace and lawful security

- `BGD23-056`: Bangladesh’s Rooppur framework includes Russian fuel provision and spent-fuel return, indicating nuclear cooperation structured through intergovernmental agreements rather than weapons activity. [IAEA national report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/24/02/cns_bangladesh_national_report_2022.pdf)
- `BGD23-057`: Bangladesh continued hosting roughly one million Rohingya refugees while regional violence and donor shortages created security and humanitarian pressure. This is a persistent policy context, not proof of a 2023 ruler-directed security failure. [World Bank development-partnership report](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2023/11/20/bangladesh-a-fifty-year-partnership-in-development-achievements)
- `BGD23-058`: The 2023 IMF resilience facility explicitly supported climate resilience and climate-financing priorities, providing a multilateral, non-military form of international cooperation. [IMF December 2023 release](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/12/12/pr23440-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2023-art-iv-consult-completes-1st-rev-ecf-eef-rsf)

Contrary/limitation: targeted searches for Bangladesh–Myanmar or Bangladesh–India military escalation in 2023 did not recover a precise Hasina-directed operation, peacekeeping decision, arms-control act, or border-restraint record. The strongest Myanmar restraint evidence found was from February 2024 and is outside the immutable period. This chapter remains evidence-short.

## 3B — Domestic safety and protection

- `BGD23-059`: By mid-November 2023, UN Special Procedures recorded approximately 10,000 opposition arrests, allegations of disappearances and detention deaths, and reported harassment of activists’ family members (communication pp. 1–2). [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-060`: The same UN communication records at least eight BNP members reportedly dying in custody after 28 October, with no independent investigations launched. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-061`: UN Special Procedures recorded reported pressure on voters by candidates and law enforcement, including threats involving loss of social-protection benefits. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-062`: The UN communication reports 56 deaths in election-related violence since 28 October, while expressly cautioning that it was not prejudging allegation accuracy. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-063`: WHO documented the Bangladesh government’s dengue response: a DGHS coordination committee, central and district control rooms, repurposed hospitals, updated clinical guidelines, supplies, surveillance, awareness campaigns, and vector-control measures. [WHO outbreak report](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2023-DON481)
- `BGD23-064`: The World Bank approved a $200 million urban-health project in August 2023, including dengue early-warning, outbreak-response capacity, primary-care facilities, and services targeted at approximately 2.5 million children under five. [World Bank release](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/08/30/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-improve-primary-healthcare-in-cities)

Contrary evidence: the government disputed arrest totals and attributed violence to BNP actors; AP records government figures of 2,000–3,000 arrests versus opposition claims around 20,000. [AP election report](https://apnews.com/article/41ab22ccaa503bbf180939ca2c5918c7)

## 4B — Political freedom and authoritarian rule

- `BGD23-065`: The 2024 election schedule was declared on 15 November 2023, with nominations, scrutiny, withdrawal, and campaign steps occurring during 2023; the poll itself was 7 January 2024. [Election chronology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bangladeshi_general_election)
- `BGD23-066`: Hasina rejected the BNP’s caretaker-government demand and stated that Bangladesh would not again allow an unelected government; this is a direct ruler position, while the caretaker change itself dates to 2011. [Election chronology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bangladeshi_general_election)
- `BGD23-067`: The United States announced a 23 May 2023 visa policy covering officials, party members, law enforcement, judiciary, and security personnel believed responsible for undermining Bangladesh’s democratic election process. [Election chronology with State Department text](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bangladeshi_general_election)
- `BGD23-068`: The UN communication records opposition boycott, reported voter pressure, arrests, deaths, and concern that the election environment undermined public participation. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-069`: Freedom House’s 2023 country report records BNP rallies during the year but also disruption, clashes, Odhikar’s registration revocation, and violence, ballot stuffing, harassment, and arrests around the election period. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2023)
- `BGD23-070`: The government’s contrary position was that the Election Commission was independent and the electoral process would remain under official and international-observer scrutiny. [Election chronology, government position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bangladeshi_general_election)

Temporal note: the January 2024 result is retained only as a clearly marked consequence of 2023 scheduling and campaign decisions, not as a 2023 event.

## 5B — Economic well-being

- `BGD23-071`: The World Bank’s October 2023 update reports extreme poverty at 5% in 2022, improved infant mortality, stunting, electricity, sanitation, and education, with faster rural poverty reduction but widening urban inequality. [World Bank update](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2023/10/05/structural-reforms-are-essential-to-sustain-growth-poverty-reduction-in-bangladesh)
- `BGD23-072`: The same update reports FY23 growth slowing to 6.0%, inflation and balance-of-payments pressure, energy and import constraints, increased government bank borrowing, and financial-sector vulnerabilities. [World Bank update](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2023/10/05/structural-reforms-are-essential-to-sustain-growth-poverty-reduction-in-bangladesh)
- `BGD23-073`: IMF’s October 2023 review records substantial reform progress but continuing pressure on the taka and foreign-exchange reserves, recommending further monetary tightening, exchange-rate flexibility, and fiscal restraint. [IMF October release](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/10/19/pr23357-imf-first-review-under-ecf-eff-rsf-concludes-2023-article-iv-consultation-with-bangladesh)
- `BGD23-074`: IMF’s December 2023 board review released approximately $468.3 million under ECF/EFF and $221.5 million under RSF; the program had completed six of seven structural benchmarks, while one financial-law benchmark was delayed. [IMF December release](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/12/12/pr23440-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2023-art-iv-consult-completes-1st-rev-ecf-eef-rsf)
- `BGD23-075`: The IMF staff report records two of three performance criteria and three of four indicative targets completed, with six of seven structural benchmarks met. [IMF staff report, pp. 2, 6–7](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2023/english/1bgdea2023003.pdf)

These sources establish measured outcomes and policy implementation, but do not by themselves prove Hasina’s personal competence, intent, or responsibility for every macroeconomic result.

## 6B — Social well-being

- `BGD23-076`: WHO records a formal Bangladesh dengue response involving national coordination, hospital repurposing, clinical guidance, surveillance, supplies, public communication, and vector control. [WHO outbreak report](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2023-DON481)
- `BGD23-077`: The World Bank’s August 2023 urban-health project targeted primary care, maternal services, hypertension screening, lower out-of-pocket costs, and dengue prevention for urban populations. [World Bank release](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/08/30/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-improve-primary-healthcare-in-cities)
- `BGD23-078`: Bangladesh officially launched its universal pension scheme on 17 August 2023. The official portal describes four schemes, online registration and payment, a government subsidy for low-income participants, and a target of broad adult coverage. [Bangladesh Universal Pension portal](https://www.upension.gov.bd/Public/PensionBriefBn)
- `BGD23-079`: A contemporaneous Daily Star explainer confirms rollout on 17 August 2023 and describes eligibility for adults aged 18–50, informal-sector participation, and the four scheme categories. [Daily Star](https://online-d11.thedailystar.net/business/news/universal-pension-scheme-all-you-need-know-3396451)
- `BGD23-080`: World Bank country data reports 2023 net primary enrollment of 93.1% and lower-secondary enrollment of 76.3%, with higher enrollment among girls. [World Bank Bangladesh profile](https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/country/bangladesh)

Contrary/limitation: WHO’s report also assesses dengue risk as high and notes health-system pressure, prolonged monsoon risk, and the limits of fogging-only approaches. [WHO outbreak report](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2023-DON481) Social outcomes therefore remain mixed and attribution-sensitive.

## 7B — Personal integrity and honesty

- `BGD23-081`: The available 2023 evidence directly documents public statements, institutional policies, and government conduct, but no reliable 2023 source establishing Hasina’s personal enrichment, asset concealment, family contracts, or direct financial benefit was recovered.
- `BGD23-082`: The IMF record documents that Bangladesh authorities completed most program benchmarks but had one delayed financial-law benchmark; this is an institutional implementation record, not personal-integrity evidence. [IMF staff report](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2023/english/1bgdea2023003.pdf)
- `BGD23-083`: The official pension portal presents the pension scheme as a government social-security initiative associated with Hasina’s long-term policy commitments; this is a government self-description and should not be treated as independent proof of honesty or ethical character. [Official pension portal](https://www.upension.gov.bd/Public/PensionBriefBn)
- `BGD23-084`: The government’s contrary position on election and rights allegations was that the Election Commission was independent and law-enforcement responses were lawful, while opposition and international bodies disputed those claims. [Government position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bangladeshi_general_election), [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)

Disposition: retain institutional and public-claim evidence, but reject any personal-enrichment or personal-concealment inference absent direct documentation.

## 8B — Effectiveness and competence

- `BGD23-085`: The IMF staff report provides a precise implementation record: six of seven structural benchmarks met, two of three performance criteria met, and three of four indicative targets met by the first review. [IMF staff report, pp. 6–7](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2023/english/1bgdea2023003.pdf)
- `BGD23-086`: The universal pension scheme was operationally launched on 17 August 2023 with four participation tracks, online registration/payment infrastructure, and a planned low-income government subsidy. [Official portal](https://www.upension.gov.bd/Public/PensionBriefBn)
- `BGD23-087`: The World Bank approved and specified an urban-health project with service targets, facilities, maternal-care goals, hypertension screening, dengue early warning, and outbreak-response capacity. [World Bank release](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/08/30/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-improve-primary-healthcare-in-cities)
- `BGD23-088`: The World Bank’s October update records both development gains and implementation constraints: poverty reduction and improved services alongside inflation, import constraints, energy shortages, financial vulnerabilities, and urban inequality. [World Bank update](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2023/10/05/structural-reforms-are-essential-to-sustain-growth-poverty-reduction-in-bangladesh)
- `BGD23-089`: The UN communication records reported arrests, deaths, voter pressure, and lack of independent investigations during the late-2023 election period, providing contrary evidence against treating state capacity or political execution as uniformly successful. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-090`: The EU’s November 2023 mission recognized progress in garment-sector safety and economic/social rights while identifying continuing shortcomings in freedom of expression, association, assembly, and civil-society conditions. [EEAS mission report](https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/bangladesh/eu-eba-monitoring-mission-bangladesh-12-16-november-2023_en)

No scoring conclusion is offered. The evidence now supports separating administrative implementation, social-program rollout, macroeconomic management, and political control rather than treating regime survival as a single effectiveness outcome.

I could not persist these additions or update the ledger manifest because the local execution environment failed before filesystem access.
